model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage for five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on the x-axis using a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale, ranging from 40% to 65%. The Base method (black line with circle markers) shows a slow increase from approximately 39% at 1 to 43% at 1000. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) starts at about 44% and rises to approximately 57% at 1000. The FT method (blue line with triangle markers) begins at 40% and increases to about 47% at 1000. The MEMIT method (purple line with cross markers) starts at around 44% and climbs to approximately 55% at 1000. The ROME method (green line with square markers) begins at about 51% and steadily increases to approximately 65% at 1000, showing the highest performance across the entire range.
